## Observation

For a Boolean relation \(H(x,w)\), fixing a prefix of \(x\) preserves an exact representation of the projected residual:
\[
L_p(z)=1 \iff \exists w\,H(pz,w)=1.
\]
Reading a bit \(b\) gives \(L_{pb}(z')=L_p(bz')\). The cofactored circuit for \(H\) uses at most its original \(h\) gates, since fixing inputs adds no gates.

This establishes a real-gate-free update for the **witness relation** when the prefix is stored explicitly. **Constructive proof attempt:** For pairwise disjoint gate supports \(S_j\), let \(c_j\) be the number of assignments on \(S_j\) making gate \(j\) true, and let \(v_j\in\mathbb Z\). Define \(l_j=\max(0,-v_j)\) and \(L=\sum_j l_j\). The polynomial
\[
P(z)=\prod_j\left((2^{|S_j|}-c_j)z^{l_j}+c_jz^{l_j+v_j}\right)
\]
has only nonnegative exponents. Choosing the true or false term for each gate encodes one truth pattern; its coefficient counts the assignments realizing that pattern, and its exponent is \(L+\sum_{j\text{ true}}v_j\). Thus the number of satisfying assignments is
\[
2^{n-\sum_j|S_j|}\sum_{e\ge T+L}[z^e]P(z).
\]
The factor outside accounts for variables in no support. This proves the identity for disjoint supports, including negative and zero weights. It is a proof attempt in this response; I did not record it in proof state.

**Observation.** For any fan-in-two circuit \(C:\{0,1\}^N\to\{0,1\}\) of size \(L\), the two completion predicates
\[
T_b(p)=1 \iff \exists z\in\{0,1\}^{N-t-1}: C(p\|b\|z)=1,\qquad b\in\{0,1\},
\]
where \(p\in\{0,1\}^t\) is variable, have a joint circuit of size at most \(2^{N-t}(L+1)-2\).

**Proof.** For each \(b\) and suffix \(z\), make a copy of \(C\), wiring \(b,z\) as constants and \(p\) to the other inputs. There are \(2^{N-t}\) copies, costing at most \(2^{N-t}L\) gates. OR the outputs separately for each \(b\); the two trees cost \(2^{N-t}-2\) gates. Each output is exactly the disjunction over suffixes defining \(T_b\).

**Scope.** This variable-prefix construction repairs the fixed-prefix issue in S0647, but its bound can be exponential in the remaining truth-table length.
